scope: S05-T01B local semantic retrieval and pgvector selection POC

selection.initial_search: exact cosine search with relational filters
selection.hnsw: validated but deferred until measured corpus size justifies approximate search

verification.red: Before implementation, pytest exited 4 because the target evaluation test file did not exist.
verification.backend_tests: 142 passed with disposable PostgreSQL 16 and RabbitMQ 4.1; 2 upstream deprecation warnings
verification.ruff: format and lint passed for all backend source, scripts and tests
verification.mypy: strict check passed for 122 source files
verification.openapi: FastAPI-generated OpenAPI snapshot check passed; this POC makes no HTTP contract change
verification.frontend: UmiOpenAPI drift, boundary, negative boundary, Prettier and TypeScript/Vite checks passed; no generated file changed
verification.dependency_audit: pip-audit found no known vulnerabilities; npm production audit found 0 vulnerabilities

limitations: The corpus and every query are explicit synthetic fixtures; the perfect score does not establish real platform recall, slang coverage or production ranking quality.
The eight-row pgvector check validates protocol and filtering, not index performance or approximate-search recall at scale.
No external platform, real account session, existing MinIO instance, paid service, production database migration, API, Swagger or frontend semantic-search control was used.
A production slice must persist model digest and input hash, define stale/deleted states, rerun a real labeled query set, and keep exact retrieval available as an explicit mode.
